topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and outlines how the session will integrate previously learned components to explain the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate Recognition of Pathogens and Cellular Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system detects microbial infections and cellular injury through pattern recognition receptors, their molecular ligands, and intracellular signaling complexes.

topics.label: Inflammatory Cascade, Cell Trafficking, and Systemic Consequences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how sentinel cell activation coordinates leukocyte recruitment into tissues, enables antigen trafficking to lymph nodes, and can produce severe systemic pathologies such as septic shock when overactivated.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the mechanisms that shut down acute inflammation, govern tissue repair, and manage persistent inflammatory conditions through adaptations such as granuloma formation.
